criteria.text: Symptomatic relief of non-infectious diarrhea in patients with HIV/AIDS on antiretroviral therapy.
Patient is 18 years of age or older.
HIV/AIDS diagnosis confirmed by antiretroviral claims within the last 90 days.
One or more watery stools daily for 5 out of 7 days per week.

Secondary causes (irritable bowel syndrome, gluten and lactose intolerance, traveler’s diarrhea, functional diarrhea, and antiretroviral therapy associated diarrhea) ruled out by complete and appropriate physical and historical examination.
Tried and failed loperamide or has a contraindication to loperamide.
Tried and failed atropine-diphenoxylate or has a contraindication to atropine-diphenoxylate.

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Mytesi (crofelemer) Criteria Version 1; effective 2021-05-24. All approval criteria are required; failure to meet approval criteria is grounds for denial.
Caution (manual review): consider infectious etiologies of diarrhea before starting treatment to reduce the risk of inappropriate therapy and worsening disease.
Authorization (manual review): initial approval up to 3 months; re-authorization up to 12 months.
Quantity limit (manual review): 60 tablets of 125 mg per 30 days.
